name: Infrax Renewable Ltd
tagline: Solar energy project developer with strong 105% ROCE, positioned in India's renewable energy growth story with government support and 500GW capacity expansion target
business_overview: Infrax Renewable develops and operates solar energy projects in India. The business model is based on long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) with utilities and corporates, providing revenue visibility. The company benefits from India's renewable energy capacity addition targets of 500GW by 2030.
fundamentals_narrative: Infrax Renewable shows strong growth trajectory with 206% revenue growth YoY (Rs 30.46 Cr in FY25 to Rs 93.2 Cr in FY26). The company maintains healthy EBITDA margins of 15.6% and demonstrates 105% ROCE, indicating efficient capital deployment. EBITDA of Rs 14.56 Cr on revenues of Rs 93.2 Cr suggests strong cash generation capability. The recently completed IPO provides capital for capacity expansion.
technical_read: Current price Rs 114 with P/E of 16x is reasonable for high-growth renewable energy company with 105% ROCE and strong sector tailwind.
sector_analysis: India renewable energy sector is one of the fastest-growing globally. Government target of 500GW renewable capacity by 2030 (up from ~200GW currently) provides multi-year growth runway. Corporate ESG commitments and PPAs are driving demand for renewable power. Renewable energy prices have declined, making projects more economically viable.
sentiment_summary: Renewable energy sector is attracting increased institutional interest. Infrax as a project developer benefits from long-term PPA revenue visibility model.
bull_case: Exceptional growth: 206% revenue growth YoY demonstrates strong project execution and capacity addition
Strong ROCE (105%) and healthy EBITDA margins (15.6%) indicate quality business economics
Multi-year growth runway: India targeting 500GW renewable capacity by 2030 with current 200GW base
Revenue visibility: Long-term PPAs (typically 20-25 years) provide revenue certainty and cash flow stability
Government support: Subsidies, tax incentives, and renewable energy credits drive project economics
Small market cap (~Rs 175 Cr) with strong growth profile leaves room for significant re-rating
bear_case: Project execution risk: Renewable energy projects face delays, cost overruns, and land acquisition challenges
Capital intensity: Business requires continuous capex for capacity addition, creating funding pressure
Regulatory risk: Changes in renewable energy policy or subsidy structures could impact project returns
PPA price risk: Long-term PPAs lock in prices that may not keep pace with inflation
New company: Limited operational history and no established track record of long-term cash generation
verdict_headline: High-growth renewable energy developer positioned in India's 500GW expansion with strong unit economics and PPA visibility - execution risk is key variable
verdict_reasoning: Four-box assessment: tailwind=VERY STRONG (renewable capacity expansion), TAM=MASSIVE (500GW target), moat=MODERATE (PPAs provide visibility but capital intensive), valuation=FAIR
206% YoY revenue growth and 105% ROCE demonstrate strong execution and capital efficiency
Long-term PPAs provide multi-year revenue visibility rare for small-cap stocks
Project execution risk and capital requirements are key risks to monitor
Small market cap provides upside optionality if company successfully scales

four_box.tailwind: VERY STRONG - India renewable capacity addition target 500GW by 2030, corporate ESG demand, declining renewable costs
four_box.tam: MASSIVE - Indian renewable energy market growing 15%+ CAGR, government committed to targets
four_box.moat: MODERATE - Long-term PPAs provide revenue visibility but project development is capital intensive and competitive
four_box.valuation: FAIR - P/E 16x for ROCE 105% and 200%+ growth is reasonable
four_box.note: Very strong tailwind and growth offset by project execution and capital intensity risks
